clue.text: Sore after returning to position in time of resettlement?

indicators.note: the sore piece comes after the position piece

parts.note: a post is a position or job

indicators.note: returning means the word for sore is read backwards

parts.note: raw means sore, as skin can be

explanation.surface: Someone sore at coming back to their old job as everyone settles down again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sore' looks like the definition, but it is the raw piece; the definition is the time after fighting ends.
explanation.definitionFit: The period after a war is when displaced people and soldiers are resettled, so the adjective fits loosely, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Vicinity with princes mixing outside court

indicators.note: outside means the shuffled letters go around the court abbreviation
mixing signals the letters of princes being stirred up

explanation.surface: Royal princes mingling outside a court in the neighbourhood.
explanation.definitionFit: Precincts are the surrounding area or environs of a place, hence its vicinity.

clue.text: Weapon of former commander needing minimal time to get loaded

indicators.note: to get loaded means the letter is packed inside the other word, as a gun is loaded

parts.note: a shogun was a hereditary military ruler of Japan
T, a single letter, is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A former commander's gun that needs barely any time to load.
explanation.definitionFit: A shotgun is a firearm that fires a spread of pellets, so a type of weapon.

clue.text: We are put outside hotel in what circumstances?

indicators.note: put outside means the contraction goes around the letter

parts.note: we're is the contraction of we are
H is Hotel in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: People asking when they will be turned out of a hotel.
explanation.definitionFit: Where can mean in which situation, as in 'where would we be without it?'

clue.text: Restrictions and rules not good

indicators.note: not means the letter is dropped from the word for rules

parts.note: reigns means rules, as a monarch does

explanation.surface: Limits and regulations that are bad.
explanation.definitionFit: Reins figuratively are controls or checks, as in keeping a tight rein on spending.

clue.text: Process making Oscar's successor sick inside

indicators.note: inside means the word for sick goes within the other piece

parts.note: in the NATO alphabet Papa follows Oscar
ill means sick

explanation.surface: Something about an Oscar winner's successor feeling queasy during the process.
explanation.walkthrough: Oscar and Papa are consecutive words in the radio alphabet for O and P.
explanation.definitionFit: In anatomy a process is a small projection, and a papilla is a tiny nipple-like protuberance such as those on the tongue.

clue.text: Mate grabbing husband with fury is a beast

indicators.note: grabbing means the friend word seizes the letter inside it

parts.note: a pal is a mate or friend
anger is fury

explanation.surface: A friend clutching her husband in rage is acting like an animal.
explanation.walkthrough: A phalanger is an Australasian marsupial such as a possum.
explanation.definitionFit: The phalanger is a tree-dwelling marsupial, an example of an animal.

clue.text: Pater, alas, coming to grief in gymnasium

indicators.note: coming to grief means ruined or broken up, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Father, sadly, having an accident at the gym.
explanation.definitionFit: A palaestra was an ancient Greek wrestling school, an exercise ground like a gym.

clue.text: Boy sailor, ultimately one becoming old-fashioned pirate?

parts.note: a lad is a boy

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word sailor

explanation.surface: A young sailor who in the end turns into a pirate of olden times.
explanation.definitionFit: A ladrone is an archaic word for a robber or bandit, sometimes a sea-robber, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Female learner diving into a river

indicators.note: diving into means the letter goes into the river word

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Scotland and in Wales
L is the learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A woman learning to swim plunging into a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Adele is a woman's name, famously the singer, so the name stands for a female.

clue.text: Special collection from East presented by lush Heather

parts.note: E is the compass abbreviation for east
a lush is a drunkard, as is a sot
Erica is the botanical genus of heather, and also a woman's name

explanation.surface: A curated collection from the East brought out by a drunken woman named Heather.
explanation.definitionFit: Esoterica are items of interest only to a select few, the kind of specialised material a collector gathers.

clue.text: Old BBC boss perhaps entertained by the French club?

indicators.note: being entertained by something means being held within it

parts.note: le is French for the
the BBC is run by its Director General, DG

explanation.surface: A former BBC chief being hosted at a French club.
explanation.definitionFit: A lodge is a branch or meeting place of a society such as the Freemasons, a kind of club.

clue.text: Artist with bit of sculpture in entrance

parts.note: Jean-Auguste-Dominique Ingres was a French painter

indicators.note: a bit of the word sculpture here is just its opening letter

explanation.surface: A painter with a fragment of a statue standing in a doorway.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingress is the act or means of going in, a formal synonym for entry.

clue.text: Like botanical feature that could win first prize at flower show?

definitions.text: Like botanical feature that could win first prize at flower show?

parts.words: Like botanical feature that could win first prize at flower show
parts.note: split into two words, the answer reads as a champion bloom, while the whole word is a botanical term for leaf shape

explanation.walkthrough: Read as ACE ROSE, it is the prize-winning flower; as one word it describes needle-shaped leaves like a pine's.
explanation.definitionFit: Acerose is a botanical adjective meaning needle-shaped, describing leaves such as those of conifers.

clue.text: Feature of carol service, with Noel finally included in prison entertainment?

parts.note: can is slang for prison

indicators.note: included in means the letter is placed within the longer piece

parts.note: delight is pleasure or entertainment

indicators.note: finally picks out only the closing letter of the name Noel

explanation.surface: A Christmas carol service featuring someone named Noel, oddly set as a prison show.
explanation.walkthrough: Noel suggests Christmas in the surface, but only its last letter is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Carol services are traditionally lit by candles, so the soft glow of candles is a hallmark of them.

clue.text: Chemical solution dissolving metal wire

indicators.note: dissolving means breaking down, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An acid bath that eats through metal wire.
explanation.definitionFit: Limewater is a solution of calcium hydroxide in water, used to test for carbon dioxide.

clue.text: More than one musician longs to cover a number one

indicators.note: to cover means the longing word goes over and around the other pieces

parts.note: lusts means longs for
ten is a number
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A performer who yearns to cover a chart-topping song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a number one' looks like a hit single, but splits into a number and one.
explanation.definitionFit: Lutenists are players of the lute, so they are instrumentalists in the plural.

clue.text: Character in Thermopylae had to retreat

indicators.note: to retreat is to go back, so the word for had is read backwards

parts.note: ate means had, as in had a meal

explanation.surface: Someone at the battle of Thermopylae who had to fall back.
explanation.walkthrough: Thermopylae is Greek, so its letters include the Greek character eta.
explanation.definitionFit: Eta is a letter of the Greek alphabet, which would spell a Greek place name like Thermopylae.

clue.text: Certain elements function inside out

parts.note: an act is a function, as in a performer's role

indicators.note: out signals the letters of inside are disordered

explanation.surface: Elements that operate in reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside out' reads as one phrase, but 'out' scrambles 'inside'.
explanation.definitionFit: The actinides are the series of radioactive chemical elements from actinium to lawrencium.

clue.text: Dry religious group, not half TT

indicators.note: not means the letter is left out of the group's word

parts.note: a sect is a religious group

indicators.note: half of the two-letter TT is a single T

explanation.surface: A teetotal religious group, only partly abstaining, is dry.
explanation.walkthrough: TT is the usual abbreviation for teetotal, which chimes with dry in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Sec is the French-derived term for dry wine, not sweet.

clue.text: Quill writer Albert used to pen his article

indicators.note: used to pen means the writer's name encloses the other piece, as a pen holds animals

parts.note: Albert Camus was a French writer
la is a French article, so Camus's own

explanation.surface: The writer Albert Camus wrote his piece with a quill.
explanation.definitionFit: Calamus is the hollow shaft of a feather, and also a reed pen, both senses of a quill.

clue.text: Starlet I aim to change, being out to make loads of money?

definitions.text: out to make loads of money?

indicators.note: to change signals the letters of the phrase being rearranged

explanation.surface: A young actress resolving to reform since she is so obsessed with money.
explanation.definitionFit: A materialist values possessions and wealth above all, so is keen on getting rich.

clue.text: American princess wants a new house hidden away

indicators.note: hidden away means the abbreviation for house is tucked inside the other letters

parts.note: Princess Ida is a Gilbert and Sullivan heroine

explanation.surface: A princess wanting a fresh home tucked out of sight.
explanation.definitionFit: An Idahoan is a native of the US state of Idaho, so an American.

clue.text: PM, nasty about Labour's leader, getting victory

indicators.note: about means the word for nasty goes round the letter

parts.note: bad means nasty

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of Labour

parts.note: a win is a victory

explanation.surface: A prime minister, cruel about the Labour leader, winning the election.
explanation.walkthrough: Stanley Baldwin was a Conservative British Prime Minister between the wars.
explanation.definitionFit: Stanley Baldwin served three times as British Prime Minister, so he is an example of a PM.

clue.text: Bishop put down as "a bit boring"?

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
to land is to put down, as an aircraft does

explanation.surface: A bishop dismissed as somewhat dull.
explanation.definitionFit: Bland means mild and lacking interest, a gentle way of saying somewhat dull.

clue.text: What's odd about wet weather bringing disease?

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: rum means odd or strange
rain is wet weather

explanation.surface: Asking what is strange about rainy weather causing illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like it means concerning, but it turns RUM round.
explanation.definitionFit: Murrain is an old word for an infectious disease of cattle, or a plague.

clue.text: Report of intellectual being unearthed

indicators.note: report of means the word is as it would be heard spoken

parts.note: the mind is the intellect

explanation.surface: A report about a thinker being exposed.
explanation.definitionFit: Mined means dug out of the ground, as coal is extracted.

clue.text: Steal and carry off firearm

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for searching and robbing a place and a noun for a long gun.

clue.text: Allow a thousand to enter passage

indicators.note: to enter means to go inside, so the numeral goes into the passage

parts.note: an adit is a horizontal passage into a mine
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: Permitting a thousand people to go into a corridor.
explanation.walkthrough: An adit is a mining term for an entrance tunnel.
explanation.definitionFit: To admit someone is to let them in, which is to allow them entry.

clue.text: Composure of celebrated female, one sitting in bar

parts.note: to sing of something is to celebrate it, so sang

indicators.note: sitting in means the numeral is placed within the word for bar

parts.note: a rod is a bar
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: The calm of a famous woman perched in a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Sang-froid, French for cold blood, is coolness and self-possession under pressure.

clue.text: Wants gentleman to have children back around

indicators.note: around means the children's word goes about the gentleman's
back means the word for children is read in reverse

parts.note: seed means offspring, as in biblical usage
sir is a title for a gentleman

explanation.surface: A gentleman wishing to have his children back with him.
explanation.definitionFit: Desires as a verb means longs for, a close synonym of wants.

clue.text: They may be given fee to hold girl back?

definitions.text: They may be given fee to hold girl back?

indicators.note: to hold means the fee word goes around the other piece

parts.note: dues are a fee or subscription

indicators.note: back means the girl's name is read backwards

parts.note: Ann is a girl's name

explanation.surface: People paid a fee to keep a young woman in check.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes chaperones paid to restrain a girl, while the second half is the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Duennas were older women employed in Spanish households as chaperones to watch over young ladies.
